problem: Prior ALFRED agents (Shridhar et al.) use a single-stream seq2seq model that predicts actions and class-agnostic pixel masks from the same concatenated vision-language features, so they generalize poorly to unseen scenes, localise objects badly, and get stuck on obstacles.
motivation: Interactive instruction following needs both global semantic cues for action prediction and pixel-level object understanding for interaction, which are semantically different tasks. Inspired by the ventral/dorsal visual streams, the authors argue they should be handled by separate streams. Also, behavior cloning on perfect expert trajectories gives no recovery behavior when the agent is blocked at inference.
key_idea: Factorize the agent into an Interactive Perception Module (object-centric class prediction plus instance mask selection) and an Action Policy Module, both with language-guided dynamic filters, plus inference-time obstruction evasion.
insight: Factorization lets each stream attend to different language (goal statement for IPM, step instructions for APM); the single stream keeps attending to the object noun regardless of action. The ablation table shows the two-stream model beats single-stream with augmentation (val-seen task 25.85 vs 22.32, val-unseen 5.36 vs 4.51). Removing OCL (deconv class-agnostic mask) collapses performance (val-seen 15.85 to 3.90), and random instance selection nearly halves performance, so correct object class and instance selection dominate success.
method: Factorized two-stream design: IPM localises interaction objects and APM predicts the action sequence, trained end-to-end with cross-entropy; the IPM receives the goal statement and the APM the step-by-step instructions.

Language-guided dynamic filters: an FC filter generator maps language features to N_DF filters that convolve ResNet-18 visual features, giving attended visual features per stream, replacing concatenation.

Object-centric localisation (target class prediction): the IPM LSTM (visual, language, previous action) predicts the target object class via FC. Masks come from a pre-trained Mask R-CNN instance segmenter.
Instance association: pick the highest-confidence instance of the predicted class when the class changes; otherwise pick the instance whose center is closest to the previous interaction mask center.
Obstruction evasion: if ||v_{t-1}-v_t||^2 < epsilon, the previous action is removed from the action space, so the next-best action is taken.
Data augmentation: color-channel swapping and AutoAugment (ImageNet policy), giving 4 augmented trajectories per original.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 (pre-trained) visual encoder + LSTM decoders + dynamic filters, trained end-to-end; pre-trained Mask R-CNN mask generator
setting.training_data: ALFRED expert demonstrations (behavior cloning), 30 epochs Adam, with color-swap and AutoAugment augmentation (5x trajectories)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 224x224 plus language (goal statement and step-by-step instructions)
setting.action_space: ALFRED discrete low-level actions (MoveAhead, Rotate, Look, Pickup, Put, Open, Close, Toggle, Slice, Stop) plus a pixel-wise interaction mask

numbers_note: ALFRED is not in the canonical benchmark list, so 'ALFRED' is used as the name. Metrics are Task SR and Goal-Cond SR with path-length-weighted (PLW) versions.
results: MOCA reaches 7.65 task SR and 15.73 goal-cond on test-unseen and 26.81 / 33.20 on test-seen, beating the ECCV-2020 challenge winner Nguyen et al. (4.45 / 12.34 unseen; 12.39 / 20.68 seen) and Shridhar et al. baseline (0.39 unseen task SR). Ablations show factorization, OCL, dynamic filters, augmentation, instance association and obstruction evasion each contribute, with OCL the largest.
limitations: Absolute unseen-scene success remains very low (about 5-8% task SR) versus 91% for humans.
Failures from navigation errors that leave the target object unseen mislead the IPM; the obstruction detector is a simple feature-difference heuristic.
Depends on a pre-trained Mask R-CNN and a fixed set of object classes, and the per-stream language inputs are hand-chosen.
